task_name: Lanternwood Folk Fest - Performer credential system
client_brief:
Performer laminates for Lanternwood, rebuilt from last year's printed artwork

Twenty-two people need correct performer laminates. Our designer left in 2024, and the usable starting point is last year's printed artwork. We need a production designer who will rebuild the run carefully, not carry last year's names or fields into new passes.

The commission

 Festival access credential: 22 named exports. The role and access areas match this person record. When a headshot is supplied, it belongs to the named person; otherwise the credential contains no invented portrait. The credential remains readable when worn.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Three stages, one field, after dark.
brand_identity.sector: An independent three stage folk and roots music festival held on a farm outside Burlington, sixth edition.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: outside Burlington, Vermont; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Lanternwood Folk Fest is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is outside Burlington, Vermont, and this commission covers phase 1: performer passes and on-sale campaign.
brand_identity.audience: A discovery led crowd aged eighteen to forty, scene literate rather than corporate, who buy on atmosphere and word of mouth and expect the field weekend to feel real rather than packaged.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Weekend general admission 145 dollars, VIP 320, roughly four thousand weekend tickets. Mid tier independent: energetic and coherent, a credible VIP tier without tipping into either luxury restraint or bargain flyer chaos.
brand_identity.typography: A bold condensed display face for the lineup and the headline nights, carrying a real hierarchy that separates headline from discovery at a glance, paired with a sturdy grotesque for body, set times and the site plan legend. The feel is poster energy, warm and a little rough, never polished.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, direct, a bit of grit. It talks up the discovery stages as loudly as the headliners and keeps sponsor and billing lines exactly as agreed. Example line the brand would write: "Gates at five. Three stages till late. Come early for the names you will be bragging about next year."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our designer left in 2024 and took the logo files. The mark now survives only as a photograph of the painted canvas banner that has hung over the main stage since 2022. There is no vector, no source file and no written type or colour spec. Last year's photography was shot by two volunteers on two cameras with no brief.
brand_identity.values: Give the discovery acts the poster space, and keep the weekend feeling like a field rather than a brand.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.

Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
